bear_case: The June 23 session has broken the structural floor that anchored the 'post-FOMC accumulation' framework: BTC's $62,255–$62,313 double-bottom — held through TWO separate Day 1 stop-clock events (June 18 and June 21) — has been breached intraday at $61,926. A double-bottom breach of this kind, on a day when all three macro gates simultaneously fail (VIX 17.53, DXY 100.90, SPX futures -1.43%), signals that the bid that absorbed both prior Day 1 events has been exhausted. The secondary bear: SK Hynix's circuit-breaker reversal from ₩3,000,000 to an estimated -12% close is the textbook pattern of a parabolic local top — the Samsung HBM4E competition reports may represent a genuine competitive acceleration (not just a market rumor) that structurally compresses the HBM market-share premium embedded in SK Hynix's ₩3.0M valuation. The tertiary bear: the June 24 Micron Q3 bar ($34.66B revenue / $19.95 EPS / gross margin >80%) is now the highest-ever consensus in Micron's history, and it arrives in the worst macro context of the post-FOMC cycle — with BTC structurally broken, KOSPI circuit breakers firing, and all three risk gates simultaneously failed. A revenue 'beat' at $34.3B (technically above the pre-revision consensus but below current $34.66B) would be interpreted as a miss in this environment and could trigger broad AI memory de-rating. June 25 PCE prints add the rate-regime tail risk: core PCE above 2.8% with VIX already above 17 would reintroduce the full multiple-compression regime at the worst possible time.
